verdicts.quote: His note on a subject is a requirement, quoted verbatim. A candidate that ignores his note is REDO.
verdicts.his_note: 2026-10-24: "make mountains look BIG/mountainous rather than just little pics of mountains." 2026-10-20: "Mountains dont look like mountains they look like farm fields or something."
verdicts.seen: At altitude 320, on Dew Horn (tile 17225), Dew Horn west (11870), Gray Crags (17028) and Twilight Crags (3331), every hilly hex carries one small peak token about half a hex across. Hundreds of identical tokens sit in a regular hex lattice. The range reads as a stippled texture laid over the ground, close to his 2026-10-20 'farm fields', not as a massif. No ridge line, no continuous silhouette and no height cue joins neighbouring tokens, so no range reads bigger than one hex. The lit/shaded split and the turn toward the substellar point cannot be seen at this size. At altitude 900, the planet cap fills about a third of the frame, the peaks are a fine grain under the settlement icons, and no mountain reads at all.

refusals.would_pass: At altitude 320 a range reads as one large landform that spans several hexes: a continuous silhouette or ridge line, faces lit and shaded in one direction that can be seen at that size, and no regular per-hex lattice. At altitude 900 the big ranges can still be seen as mountains between the icons.

smallest_fix.what: Do the redraw specified in MOUNTAINS_REDRAW_BIG_NOT_LITTLE_PICS (options A range mesh, B oversized back-to-front peaks 2-3x a hex, C relief film), which he allowed to bleed over neighbouring hexes (2026-10-24). The cheapest first try is option B on the existing RM_WorldPeaks code: raise the size tunables (sizeMountains 1.32, sizeImpassable 1.42) toward 2-3, thin the cells so not every hex stamps, and sort back to front. That needs a live look at 320 and 900, not a full redesign.

refusals.criterion_why: His own words name the outcome (BIG, not little pictures; not farm fields). A drawn range that spans hexes is attainable: the code already has size tunables and he allowed overlap into neighbouring hexes.
